metadata.description: Personal Status Laws for Lebanon's 18 recognized religious communities. Article 9 of the Constitution guarantees each community's right to its own personal status law. There is no optional civil personal status code.
metadata.notes: Lebanon has 18 officially recognized religious communities, each with its own personal status laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, child custody, and adoption. These laws derive from various sources: Ottoman-era regulations, French Mandate decrees, religious authority codes, and parliamentary legislation. There is no civil marriage law in Lebanon - all marriages must be performed under a religious authority (though civil marriages performed abroad are recognized).

framework_laws.official_number: Law No. 24 of February 13, 1948 (Druze Personal Status Law)
framework_laws.official_title_arabic: قانون الأحوال الشخصية للطائفة الدرزية - قانون رقم 24/1948
framework_laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 24/1948 - Statut Personnel de la Communauté Druze
framework_laws.historical_context: The only fully codified sectarian personal status law enacted by the Lebanese Parliament (rather than by a religious authority). Governs marriage, divorce, custody, inheritance, and guardianship for the Druze community. Notable for prohibiting polygamy and establishing relatively progressive provisions compared to other religious community laws.
